title: Why you would never stop falling on Jupiter
description: Experience the terrifying descent into Jupiter, where gravity crushes you into a metallic liquid hotter than the Sun.

shots.narration: You are falling into a world where the ground simply does not exist.
Jupiter offers no solid surface to break your descent, only a bottomless plunge.
In 1995, the Galileo probe pierced these clouds faster than a speeding comet.
It braved a white-hot friction twice as intense as the surface of the Sun.
Sideways winds whip your body, tossing you through the ammonia haze at hurricane speeds.
The atmosphere soon thickens, pressing inward until it crushes everything you are.
Deep below, the gas transforms, becoming a vast, shoreless ocean of liquid hydrogen.
Eventually, the fluid grows so dense it suspends you like a floating cork.
Weight from above squeezes the hydrogen until it turns into an exotic, conductive metal.
This metallic sea simmers, radiating heat far fiercer than the Sun’s visible face.
The planet’s rapid spin churns this metal, generating a colossal, invisible magnetic field.
At the very center, the pressure equals millions of Earth atmospheres combined.
Jupiter’s core is no solid rock, but a fuzzy, dissolved soup of heavy elements.
Everything here remains trapped in a lightless world that has no bottom.
You are left suspended forever in a boiling, metallic dark.
You have fallen into a world where the ground simply does not exist.

craft.shape_brief: Tell it through a real event and the people who saw it (a mission, a storm, a night in 1859), present tense, then what it means for us now.
craft.hook_brief: two facts that cannot both be true, placed side by side

editor_notes: Replaced list-like descriptions with sensory imagery and connected the physics of the core to the 'no floor' theme for a more resonant narrative arc.
